content.text:
Do you mean **Medi-Cal in California**?

**Medi-Cal** is California’s Medicaid program. It provides **free or low-cost health coverage** for eligible California residents, including many low-income adults, children, pregnant people, seniors, and people with disabilities. ([ca.gov](https://www.ca.gov/departments/217/?utm_source=openai))

You can **apply for Medi-Cal** in a few ways:

1. **Online through Covered California** — the application can route you to Medi-Cal if you qualify. ([dhcs.ca.gov](https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/services/medi-cal-resources/medi-cal-eligibility-division/apply-for-medi-cal-or-other-affordable-quality-health-coverage/?utm_source=openai))  
2. **Through your county social services office**  
3. **By paper application** through the California Department of Health Care Services. ([dhcs.ca.gov](https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/medi-cal/apply/?utm_source=openai))  
4. **By phone** through Covered California at **1-800-300-1506**. ([ca.gov](https://www.ca.gov/agency/?item=department-of-health-care-services&utm_source=openai))

Medi-Cal generally covers doctor visits, hospital care, prescriptions, preventive care, mental health services, and many people receive coverage through a **managed care plan**. ([sfhsa.org](https://www.sfhsa.org/services/health/medi-cal/use-medi-cal?utm_source=openai))

As of **January 1, 2026**, California has a freeze on **new enrollments for certain undocumented adults** who do not have a satisfactory immigration status for federal full-scope Medi-Cal, according to CA.gov/DHCS information. ([ca.gov](https://www.ca.gov/departments/217/services/37/?utm_source=openai))

If you tell me what you need — **apply, check eligibility, renew, find a doctor, cancel Medi-Cal, report income, or fix a problem** — I can help with the next steps.
